title: The point-count zeta series
statement:
Let $k_0=\Fq$ be a finite field of characteristic $p$ and cardinality $q$ [def-weil-finite-field-q-elements], with algebraic closure
$k=\Fbar$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $X_0$ be a $k_0$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-scheme-over-base]. For $n\ge1$ let $\Fqn$ be the
degree-$n$ extension of $k_0$ (the splitting field of $T^{q^{n}}-T$ over
$k_0$), realized as the subfield $\{a\in k:a^{q^n}=a\}$ of [lem-weil-unique-subfield-of-closure]. Here the splitting field means the field generated over $k_0$ by all roots of that polynomial. Put

$$
N_n(X_0)=\#X_0(\Fqn)=\#\operatorname{Hom}_{k_0}(\Spec\Fqn,X_0),
$$

Here $\operatorname{Spec}$ is the affine spectrum [def-weil-affine-spectrum], the Hom set is the field-valued point set [def-weil-field-valued-points], and its number of elements is taken to be $0$ if this set is infinite.
Define the *zeta series*

$$
Z(X_0,T)=\exp\Bigl(\sum_{n\ge1}N_n(X_0)\frac{T^{n}}{n}\Bigr)
\in 1+T\Q[[T]],
$$

Here $\Q[[T]]$ is the ring of formal power series [def-weil-formal-power-series], and $\exp$ is the formal power-series exponential [def-weil-power-series-exponential], applied to the series with constant coefficient $0$ and coefficient $N_n/n$ in degree $n\geq1$.
For a closed point $x\in|X_0|$ [def-weil-closed-points], let $\kappa(x)$ be its residue field with its $k_0$-algebra structure induced by $X_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ [def-weil-residue-field], and put $\deg(x)=[\kappa(x):k_0]$, with value $0$ when this vector-space dimension is infinite [def-weil-closed-point-degree].

A priori $Z$ only lies in $1+T\Q[[T]]$. The point counts are recovered from
$Z$ by the logarithmic derivative, where $(\sum_{m\geq0}c_mT^m)'=\sum_{m\geq1}mc_mT^{m-1}$ and division by $Z$ means multiplication by its formal inverse, $T\,Z'/Z=\sum_{n\ge1}N_nT^{n}$; the
coefficients of $Z$ itself are *not* the $N_n$ (for instance
$[T^{2}]Z=(N_1^{2}+N_2)/2$, which for the projective line $\mathbf P^{1}_{\Fq}$ [sk-d-lines] is $q^{2}+q+1$
while $N_2=q^{2}+1$). That $Z$ has integer coefficients is not automatic for
the exponential of an arbitrary integer sequence ($N_1=1$, $N_n=0$ for
$n\ge2$ gives $\exp(T)$); for $X_0$ of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] it follows from the
closed-point Euler product of [prop-euler-product].

proof.text: The extension field used in the definition exists: [lem-weil-unique-subfield-of-closure] supplies the subfield $E_n=\{a\in k:a^{q^n}=a\}$, containing $k_0$, with $q^n$ elements. It contains all roots of $T^{q^n}-T$ in $k$ and every element of $E_n$ is such a root; consequently it is exactly the field generated by these roots, the indicated splitting field. It has degree $n$: choose a maximal linearly independent subset of the finite set $E_n$ over $k_0$. It spans (otherwise one can add an element), so if its size is $d$ [def-weil-vector-space-dimension], unique basis coordinates give $q^d=\#E_n=q^n$. Since $q>1$, $d=n$. No scheme finiteness assumption occurs here.

source.place: first paragraph: the degree-n extension as a splitting field

proof.text: For the structure map $f:X_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$, [def-weil-field-valued-points] gives precisely the maps $g:\operatorname{Spec}E_n\to X_0$ satisfying $f\circ g=\operatorname{Spec}(k_0\hookrightarrow E_n)$. Take the finite cardinality of this set, or $0$ when it is infinite, as explicitly stipulated in the item. This defines $N_n$ for every scheme, with no claim of finiteness. Independently, [def-weil-residue-field] gives the field map $k_0\to\kappa(x)$, and [def-weil-closed-point-degree] defines its natural degree, including value $0$ for infinite dimension. Thus the degree clause also makes sense for an arbitrary $X_0$.

source.place: point-count display, infinite-cardinality convention, and closed-point-degree sentence

proof.text: Put $u_n=N_n/n$ for $n\geq1$ and $U=\sum_{n\geq1}u_nT^n$. The formal exponential of [def-weil-power-series-exponential] defines $Z=\sum_{r\geq0}U^r/r!$ coefficient by coefficient: $U^r$ has no terms of degree less than $r$, so each coefficient is a finite sum. In particular $c_0=[T^0]Z=1$, and for $m\geq1$ its coefficient is $c_m=\sum_{r=1}^m(r!)^{-1}\sum_{n_1+\cdots+n_r=m,\ n_j\geq1}\prod_j u_{n_j}$. This is an actual construction with rational coefficients, and proves the displayed membership $Z\in1+T\Q[[T]]$.

source.place: zeta-series display and sentence specifying the formal exponential

proof.text: The logarithmic derivative is a direct finite-coefficient calculation. In the coefficient formula of step 3 [def-weil-power-series-exponential], multiply by $m=\sum_j n_j$. Symmetry of the $r$ positions replaces that sum by $r n_1$; cancel $r/r!=1/(r-1)!$, and sum first over $i=n_1$. This gives, for every $m\geq1$, $m c_m=\sum_{i=1}^m i u_i c_{m-i}=\sum_{i=1}^m N_i c_{m-i}$; the case $r=1$ uses the empty product $c_0=1$. All sums are finite. By the convolution definition of multiplication [def-weil-formal-power-series] these identities, together with zero constant terms on both sides, are exactly $TZ'=(\sum_{i\geq1}N_iT^i)Z$. Since $c_0=1$ is a unit in $\Q$, [lem-weil-power-series-unit-constant-coefficient] makes $Z$ invertible; multiplication by its inverse gives $TZ'/Z=\sum_{i\geq1}N_iT^i$.

source.place: last paragraph: recovery of point counts by logarithmic derivative

proof.text: The coefficient formula [def-weil-power-series-exponential] at $m=2$ has only the tuples $(2)$ and $(1,1)$, so $c_2=u_2+u_1^2/2=(N_2+N_1^2)/2$. For $\mathbf P^1_{k_0}$, [sk-d-lines] gives the chart $\operatorname{Spec}k_0[t]$, whose complement is the one point $\infty$, and the second chart $\operatorname{Spec}k_0[z]$, which contains $\infty$ as the point $z=0$. Let $E_n/k_0$ be the field of step 1 and $g:\operatorname{Spec}E_n\to\mathbf P^1_{k_0}$ a $k_0$-morphism. Its source has one point, so its image is one point, and a morphism whose image lies in an open subscheme factors uniquely through that open subscheme (the open immersion is a monomorphism onto its image). If the image lies in the first chart, [def-weil-affine-spectrum] identifies $g$ with a $k_0$-algebra map $k_0[t]\to E_n$, and these are in bijection with $E_n$ by the image of $t$: $q^n$ maps by [lem-weil-unique-subfield-of-closure]. If the image is $\infty$, $g$ factors through the second chart and is given by a $k_0$-algebra map $\varphi:k_0[z]\to E_n$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] whose image point is the prime $\varphi^{-1}(0)=(z)$; so $\varphi(z)=0$, and there is exactly one such map. The two cases are disjoint because $\infty$ is not in the first chart. Thus $N_n=q^n+1$. Substitute $N_1=q+1$ and $N_2=q^2+1$ to obtain $c_2=((q+1)^2+q^2+1)/2=q^2+q+1$. The arbitrary integer sequence $N_1=1$, $N_n=0$ for $n\geq2$ instead gives $U=T$ and $c_2=1/2$, so integrality is not automatic. The final sentence of the statement, integrality for $X_0$ of finite type, is a forward pointer to the statement node prop-euler-product, which states it for the finite-type zeta series; it is not a proof dependency of this definition, since that unit's route passes through this definition and a dependency would close a cycle.

source.place: last paragraph: the second coefficient, projective-line example, and exp(T) counterexample

proof_origin.place: Definition and explanatory final paragraph; explicit coefficient calculations supplied by Q24, using the cited existing DAG statements.
